brief.headline: KOSPI memory rout: Samsung -6.4%, SK Hynix -9.9% as Broadcom guidance triggers AI bubble concerns; HBM fundamentals intact
brief.summary: <cite index="42-1,42-9">Samsung Electronics fell 6.4% to 329,000 won while SK Hynix plunged 9.92% to 2.07 million won</cite>, driven by <cite index="42-3">Broadcom's disappointing AI business guidance triggering selling pressure in global AI and semiconductor sectors</cite>. <cite index="43-6">The Korea Exchange triggered the KOSPI circuit breaker after KOSPI 200 futures fell 5%</cite>, with <cite index="43-13">foreign investors net selling approximately $22 billion since May, including about $12 billion in SK Hynix alone</cite>. <cite index="4-13">HBM3E is expected to account for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026</cite>, while <cite index="15-1,15-11">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices surged 90-95% QoQ and NAND Flash 55-60% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="22-2">Hyperscaler capex is set to reach $725 billion in 2026</cite>, supporting multi-year demand visibility despite short-term sentiment volatility.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral to marginally long SK Hynix vs Samsung. <cite index="4-15">SK Hynix maintains 62% HBM market share as of Q2 2025 and 57% revenue share as of Q3</cite>, versus <cite index="2-9">Samsung at 35-40%</cite>. <cite index="4-21">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 for NVIDIA's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="6-1">Goldman reports Samsung's HBM3E price is 5% lower than SK Hynix's</cite>, signaling price competition to regain share. However, <cite index="9-4">Samsung provides more than 60% of Google's HBM shipments in 2025 through Broadcom</cite>, offering hyperscaler diversification. Today's relative underperformance (SK Hynix -9.9% vs Samsung -6.4%) reflects foreign liquidation of crowded positioning in the purer HBM play; near-term volatility favors Samsung's valuation buffer, but SK Hynix's technical lead and NVIDIA sole-sourcing for HBM4 justify the premium through 2H26. Watch Samsung's HBM4 qualification timeline and any Nvidia supply diversification commentary.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="15-1,15-11">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ, NAND Flash 55-60% QoQ</cite>; <cite index="16-2,16-7">Q2 2026 forecasts show DRAM up 58-63% QoQ and NAND Flash 70-75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="11-15">Counterpoint confirmed memory prices surged 80-90% QoQ from Q4 2025 into Q1 2026 across most segments</cite>. <cite index="10-9">DRAM manufacturers are reallocating advanced process nodes toward server DRAM and HBM to support AI server demand</cite>. <cite index="3-10">The ASP gap between HBM3E and DDR5 is expected to narrow significantly in 2026</cite>, while <cite index="3-1,3-8">analysts warn HBM prices could enter a correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands</cite>. Supply remains constrained through 2026; pricing power persists but momentum is decelerating from Q1 extremes. HBM mix enrichment offsets conventional DRAM ASP pressure.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-12">Samsung and SK Hynix are prioritizing ramping HBM4 production, keeping HBM3E supply tight and lagging demand</cite>. <cite index="5-1">HBM3 costs ~$200 per 24GB stack, HBM3E ~$300 per 36GB stack, HBM4 expected at ~$500 per 48GB stack as of April 2026</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Demand for HBM3E exceeded expectations following approval for NVIDIA's H200 AI chip exports to China, with each H200 incorporating six stacks of HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="1-8,1-10">Google's TPU and Amazon's Trainium equipped with HBM3E are scheduled to begin shipments in 2026; Google's 7th-gen TPU integrates eight HBM3E stacks per chip, Amazon's Trainium3 uses four</cite>. <cite index="5-13">Lead times for HBM3E stacks remain at 20-26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="31-2,31-6">A surge of AI and HPC orders from NVIDIA, Google, Amazon, and MediaTek has driven TSMC's entire CoWoS lineup to full capacity, with both CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked</cite>. <cite index="30-8,30-9">TSMC is scaling CoWoS capacity from approximately 35,000 wafers per month in late 2024 to a projected 130,000 wafers per month by close of 2026; NVIDIA reportedly secures over 60% of total CoWoS capacity for 2025 and 2026</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung -6.4%, SK Hynix -9.9% on Broadcom-led global chip selloff
news_pulse.implication: Broadcom's AI guidance miss triggered circuit breaker; foreign outflows ($22B since May, $12B in Hynix) reflect crowded positioning unwind. Retail bid absorbed 585B won of leverage products today—sentiment stabilization vs capitulation TBD.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI triggers circuit breaker as index plunges 6% intraday
news_pulse.implication: Samsung and SK Hynix account for >50% of KOSPI weight; concentration risk materializing. Single-stock 2x ETFs down 20%; Korean regulators reviewing leverage product impact. Volatility regime shift underway.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725B, up from $670B estimate
news_pulse.implication: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft collectively planning $725B in 2026 infrastructure spend. Demand side intact; selloff is sentiment/positioning, not fundamental demand destruction. Supports memory ASP resilience through 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices forecast +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Sequential pricing momentum decelerating from Q1's record 90-95% DRAM gain but still extreme. NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle. Enterprise SSD allocation crowding out consumer; Samsung/Hynix gross margin tailwinds persist.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix holds 62% HBM share Q2 2025, 57% revenue Q3; Samsung 35-40%
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix dominance in HBM3E/HBM4 validates premium valuation. UBS sees 70% Hynix share in HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin. Samsung's 5% HBM3E price discount signals share gain attempts; watch for qualification announcements.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity scaling to 130K wpm by end-2026 from 35K late-2024
news_pulse.implication: Packaging bottleneck easing but still tight; NVIDIA locked >60% of 2025-26 capacity. CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked per Dec 2025 reports. HBM demand gated by packaging through 1H26; relief coming 2H but lead times still 20-26 weeks.

news_pulse.headline: HBM3E prices expected -28% YoY in 2026 ($15/GB to $10/GB) per Goldman
news_pulse.implication: HBM ASP compression ahead as capacity ramps and HBM4 mix shifts. However, HBM4 commands ~40% premium over HBM3E, offsetting blended ASP pressure. Samsung pricing 5% below Hynix suggests competitive intensity rising. Monitor quarterly ASP disclosure.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix rally surpassed IT bubble gains at +798% from 500-day low
news_pulse.implication: Jefferies notes bubbles extend leadership of top performers; retail participation strong but volatility increasing. Today's action consistent with March vol spike. Barclays raised PTs today citing LTA focus and supply tightness through end-2027.

brief.derivatives_signal: Volatility regime change confirmed. <cite index="40-15,40-19">SK Hynix single-stock 2x leverage ETFs fell 20%+ today, hitting all-time lows since launch</cite>; <cite index="40-22">retail investors net-purchased 585B won ($394.6B Hynix + $190.7B Samsung leverage products) into the decline</cite>. <cite index="40-21">Negative compounding effect in leveraged products will amplify losses if volatility persists</cite>. Implied vol likely spiking; options skew shifting. Korean regulators reviewing leverage product impact per Seoul Economic Daily. Near-term: continued two-way violent moves likely until foreign selling exhausts or fundamental catalyst (earnings pre-announcement, hyperscaler order commentary) stabilizes sentiment. Tactically, fade retail leverage accumulation; structurally, vol-selling strategies now higher risk.
